sections.section_title: The Strong Bear the Weak -- The Pattern of Christ
sections.summary: Paul identifies himself with the 'strong' and states their obligation to bear the weaknesses of the weak rather than pleasing themselves, grounding this in Christ's own pattern of self-denial (Psalm 69:9); scriptures produce endurance and encouragement for hope, and Paul prays that God may grant the community harmony 'in accord with Christ Jesus' so they might glorify God 'with one voice.'

sections.section_title: Mutual Welcome -- Christ's Ministry to Jew and Gentile, the Scriptural Chain
sections.summary: Paul commands mutual welcome 'as Christ has welcomed you, for the glory of God,' explaining that Christ served both the circumcised (to confirm God's promises to the patriarchs) and the Gentiles (to bring them to glorify God for his mercy), supported by four scriptural quotations from the Psalms, Torah, and Prophets demonstrating that Gentile praise alongside Israel was always God's plan; the section closes with a prayer that the God of hope would fill them with joy and peace in believing, overflowing in hope by the Spirit's power.

sections.section_title: Paul's Apostolic Ministry to the Gentiles -- The Priestly Service of the Gospel
sections.summary: Paul describes his apostolic vocation in priestly and sacrificial language -- he is a leitourgos of Christ Jesus performing hierourgia with the gospel, presenting the Gentile community as an offering sanctified by the Holy Spirit -- and explains his missionary policy of preaching where Christ has not yet been named, fulfilling Isaiah 52:15, from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum.

sections.section_title: Paul's Travel Plans -- Rome, Spain, and the Collection for Jerusalem
sections.summary: Paul explains his delayed visit to Rome, his intention to pass through on the way to Spain, and his present obligation to deliver to Jerusalem the collection from Macedonia and Achaia -- a material sharing that embodies the Gentile churches' spiritual debt to the Jewish community that provided them the gospel.

sections.section_title: The Appeal for Prayer -- The Dangers Ahead
sections.summary: Paul appeals for the community's prayers through the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of the Spirit for his safety from unbelievers in Judea and for the Jerusalem saints' acceptance of the collection, expressing hope for a joyful visit to Rome by God's will, and closing with the benediction 'the God of peace be with you all.'
